summary: Implementation phase -- the first 110-series phase to touch src/pcae/. Implements a passive Runtime Registry prototype that owns, queries, and validates plugin metadata only; no plugin loading, plugin instantiation, plugin invocation, dependency injection, or execution capability introduced. Freezes a new principle alongside 110C's Discoverable always: Metadata precedes behavior. Adds src/pcae/core/runtime_registry.py: PluginDescriptor (a frozen, inert data record -- plugin id, plugin type, version, capability list, lifecycle state, health state, implementation status, manifest, mapping onto 110B/110C contract fields) and RuntimeRegistry (a passive in-memory metadata store -- one private dict, no I/O, no subprocess, no network, no dynamic import). Implements five of 110D's nine canonical Registry API operations, metadata-only: register_metadata() (fails closed, never raises, rejects duplicate IDs and invalid descriptors without storing anything), list_plugins(), list_capabilities(), find_capability() (the unfiltered ListCapabilityProviders() view), get_plugin_metadata(). Deliberately does not implement UnregisterPlugin(), ResolveCapability() (requires Runtime-side selection behavior), GetPluginHealth() as a live signal, or ValidateCompatibility() as a gating check -- each would be behavior, not metadata, and their absence is enforced directly by tests (hasattr checks). Introspection supported without a new CLI command (permitted by the phase brief): list_plugins(), get_plugin_metadata(), list_capabilities(), find_capability(), and registry_health() (returns a RegistrySnapshot -- plugin/capability counts, registry status, aggregate metadata validity, no behavioral health field). validate_descriptor() is a pure function checking plugin_id presence, plugin_type/lifecycle_state/health_state/implementation_status against frozen vocabularies (implemented never permitted), semantic version format, duplicate capability declarations, enforce/execute hard-rejected as undeclarable, and manifest/descriptor field consistency; shared by register_metadata() (pre-store admission gate) and RuntimeRegistry.validate_consistency() (post-store read-only re-scan, RegistryValidationReport) so admission and audit can never drift apart -- proven directly by tests attempting duplicate/invalid registrations and confirming the report stays clean. Added docs/PHASE_110_RUNTIME_REGISTRY_PROTOTYPE.md. docs/ROADMAP.md evaluated and found to already state the relevant long-term vision (110B) completely -- no change made, matching 110C's/110D's own evaluation outcome. 111 new tests (tests/test_runtime_registry_prototype.py): functional coverage of every objective plus module-isolation tests mirroring 108A's isolation guarantee for permission_broker_foundation.py -- an AST-based import allowlist restricting the module to __future__/re/dataclasses/typing, and source-text scans confirming no subprocess, os.system, eval, exec, __import__, file I/O, or network call appears anywhere in the file. Focused tests (701), governance/autonomy group (1909), and the release/lifecycle regression subset actually present (1429/1429, excluding one nonexistent file and the two known-slow phase85/phase87 integration files) all passed under -n auto; fast_green 4390/4390 (matches documented baseline).
